title: SSC CHSL 2023 Tier-1 Art & Culture PART-4

questions.question: Pola festival is associated with which of the following states?
questions.solution: The Pola festival is a thanksgiving festival celebrated by farmers in Maharashtra and Chhattisgarh to acknowledge the importance of bulls and oxen in agriculture. The animals are decorated with ornaments, shawls, and paint, and are paraded through the village.

questions.question: Pawl Kut is a thanksgiving festival of which Indian state?
questions.solution: Pawl Kut is a major post-harvest thanksgiving festival in Mizoram. It is celebrated to thank the gods for a bountiful harvest and involves community feasts, traditional dances, and singing.

questions.question: Pongal is a festival of which state?
questions.solution: Pongal is a four-day harvest festival celebrated in Tamil Nadu. It is dedicated to the Sun God (Surya) and marks the beginning of Uttarayan. The tradition involves boiling rice in a pot until it overflows, symbolizing prosperity.

questions.question: Pushkar Mela is a popular cultural festival of which state?
questions.solution: The Pushkar Mela (Pushkar Camel Fair) is a world-famous cultural and livestock fair held in Rajasthan. It takes place annually in the town of Pushkar on the banks of the Pushkar Lake during the Kartik Purnima period.

questions.question: Of which of the following states is Jallikattu a famous bull-taming festival?
questions.solution: Jallikattu is a traditional bull-taming sport and festival celebrated in Tamil Nadu as part of the Mattu Pongal festivities. It involves releasing a bull into a crowd of people who attempt to grab its hump and hang on for a certain distance.

questions.question: Kerala is famous for which of the following festivals?
questions.solution: Onam is the most significant harvest festival of Kerala. It marks the legendary homecoming of King Mahabali and is celebrated with Pookalam (floral carpets), Vallam Kali (boat races), and the grand Sadhya feast.

questions.question: The famous Rath Yatra, Car Festival is associated with which Lord?
questions.solution: The world-famous Rath Yatra (Chariot Festival) held in Puri, Odisha, is dedicated to Lord Jagannath, along with his siblings Lord Balabhadra and Goddess Subhadra. The deities are taken from the Jagannath Temple to the Gundicha Temple in massive chariots.

questions.question: Gugga Naumi festival is celebrated in which of the following states?
questions.solution: Gugga Naumi is a religious festival celebrated in Haryana and parts of Rajasthan and Punjab. It is dedicated to the worship of Gugga Peer (the Snake God) to protect devotees from snake bites.

questions.question: Kajari festival is celebrated in which of the following states?
questions.solution: The Kajari (or Kajli) festival is a significant cultural event in Chhattisgarh and parts of Uttar Pradesh/Bihar. In Chhattisgarh, it is often celebrated by farmers to mark the beginning of the sowing season, accompanied by the singing of folk songs.

questions.question: Which of the following festivals is celebrated on the Makar Sankranti day in Assam?
questions.solution: Magh Bihu, also known as Bhogali Bihu, is celebrated in Assam during mid-January, coinciding with Makar Sankranti. It is a harvest festival characterized by community feasts and the burning of Mejis (bamboo structures).

questions.question: Which of the following is the famous festival of Andhra Pradesh?
questions.solution: Bonalu is a traditional Hindu festival celebrated in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana (specifically Hyderabad and Secunderabad). It is dedicated to Goddess Mahakali and involves offering 'Bonum' (cooked rice with jaggery and milk) in brass pots.

questions.question: Mopin is an agricultural festival celebrated in the state of _________.
questions.solution: Mopin is the most important agricultural festival of the Galo tribe of Arunachal Pradesh. It is celebrated to drive away evil spirits and seek blessings for a prosperous harvest and universal well-being.

questions.question: Tulip Festival is famous in which city?
questions.solution: The Tulip Festival is an annual event held at the Indira Gandhi Memorial Tulip Garden in Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir. It is the largest tulip garden in Asia and attracts tourists globally during the spring bloom.

questions.question: Since 2004, which of the following states in India is the permanent venue of the International Film Festival of India?
questions.solution: Goa has been the permanent venue for the International Film Festival of India (IFFI) since 2004. The festival aims to provide a common platform for cinemas of the world to project their excellence.

questions.question: Gaan-Ngali is a five-day festival primarily celebrated in which part of India?
questions.solution: Gaan-Ngai is a major post-harvest festival of the Zeliangrong people (Zeme, Liangmai, and Rongmei tribes) primarily in Manipur and other North-Eastern states. It is a festival of thanksgiving and welcoming the new year.

questions.question: Hornbill festival is celebrated in which of the following states?
questions.solution: The Hornbill Festival, often called the 'Festival of Festivals', is held annually from December 1st to 10th in Nagaland. It showcases the diverse cultural heritage and traditions of the various Naga tribes at the Kisama Heritage Village.

questions.question: Chaitrual and Phulaich are the festivals of which of the following states?
questions.solution: Chaitrual and Phulaich are important festivals of Himachal Pradesh. Phulaich is a festival of flowers celebrated in the Kinnaur district, while Chaitrual is observed in the Sirmaur region as a local new year festival.

questions.question: Rajini Gabra and Harni Gabra are the cultural festivals of which of the following Indian states?
questions.solution: Rajini Gabra and Harni Gabra are cultural festivals celebrated by the Dimasa community in Assam. These festivals are ritualistic ceremonies performed to seek protection for crops and the community from diseases and natural calamities.

questions.question:
With reference to Sonepur Cattle fair, consider the following statements and select the correct option:
a) It is associated with the Hariharanatha temple.
b) It begins on Purnima (full moon night) and Kartik month.
(c) It is celebrated in the Madhya Pradesh state.
questions.solution: Regarding the Sonepur Cattle Fair, statements a and b are correct. It is held at the confluence of the Ganges and Gandak rivers in Bihar (not MP), associated with the Hariharanatha temple, and starts on Kartik Purnima.

questions.question: Ambubachi fair is held every year in which of the following states?
questions.solution: The Ambubachi Mela is held annually at the Kamakhya Temple in Guwahati, Assam. It celebrates the yearly menstruation of the Goddess Kamakhya and is often referred to as the 'Mahakumbh of the East'.

questions.question: Sheorinarayan fair is held in which of the following states?
questions.solution: The Sheorinarayan Fair is a significant religious and cultural event held in the Janjgir-Champa district of Chhattisgarh. It takes place at the historic Sheorinarayan temple during Magh Purnima.

questions.question:
Match the following statements:
List I List II
a) Champakkulam boat race i) Gujarat
b) Somnath fair ii) Haryana
(c) Surajkund fair iii) Rajasthan
d) Baneshwar fair iv) Kerala
questions.option_4: a-iv, b- ii, c- i, d-iii
questions.solution: Match the Columns: The Champakkulam boat race is held in Kerala; the Somnath fair takes place in Gujarat; the Surajkund fair (International Crafts Mela) is in Haryana; and the Baneshwar fair is a tribal fair in Rajasthan.

questions.question: Simbhastha fair is held in Ujjain on the bank of which river?
questions.solution: The Simhastha Kumbh Mela is held in Ujjain once every 12 years on the banks of the Kshipra River. It is one of the four venues in India where the Kumbh Mela is celebrated.

questions.question: Kumbh Mela and Sangam are famous in which state?
questions.solution: The Kumbh Mela and the holy Sangam (the confluence of the rivers Ganga, Yamuna, and the mythical Saraswati) are world-famous attractions in Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh.

questions.question: Bastar Dussehra is celebrated in which of the following states?
questions.solution: Bastar Dussehra is a unique festival celebrated in the Bastar region of Chhattisgarh. Unlike the standard Dussehra, it lasts for 75 days and is dedicated to Danteshwari Devi, the presiding deity of the region.
